title: Wren and the Witness
premise: Kestrel Iversen, host of the podcast 'Cold Ledger', receives a confession to the 1994 disappearance of Judge Marlowe Voss — postmarked the day after the funeral of the letter's sender, retired detective Anselm Rook. Digging in, Kestrel discovers Rook covered up the crime to protect the Voss family's heir, and that the confession was meant to reach not him but the true heir: Wren Voss, a young woman raised unaware of her inheritance. As Kestrel and Wren unravel alibis woven thirty years ago, they realize someone inside the Voss estate is still killing to keep the fortune — and the will — intact. The story ends when Kestrel exposes the surviving conspirator at the reading of the second will, and Wren, refusing both the money and the courts, chooses to fund the victims' families instead, finding justice outside the law.
about_author: Ulyana Dunmore is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent two decades transcribing testimony before turning to fiction. She lives in a coastal town where fog rolls in early, and writes mysteries about the lies people tell to protect what they inherit.

chapters.title: The Postmark Problem
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A confession letter to the 1994 Voss disappearance arrives, postmarked the day after its sender's funeral. Kestrel, jaded by dead-end cases, feels the old thrill and the old dread. Emotional beat: the hook of a mystery that shouldn't be possible.

chapters.title: Anselm Rook's Last Tape
chapters.summary: Kestrel visits Rook's empty house and finds a dictaphone hidden in a wall, half a confession, cut off mid-sentence. POV: Kestrel. Beat: dread — someone searched the house before him, and recently.

chapters.title: The Girl Named Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A young estate archivist, Wren Voss, finds her own name in Rook's sealed papers and learns she is the judge's granddaughter, raised in secret. Beat: vertigo of a stolen identity.

chapters.title: Alibis in Amber
chapters.summary: Kestrel reconstructs the night of the disappearance: four witnesses, four perfect alibis, all too perfect. POV: Kestrel. Beat: the pattern of orchestration emerges — someone built the lie brick by brick.

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't Read
chapters.summary: Wren discovers the original 1994 will was replaced days after the judge's death, cutting out an entire branch of the family. POV: Wren. Beat: inheritance as weapon.

chapters.title: Cold Ledger, Warm Lead
chapters.summary: Kestrel airs an oblique episode; within hours, a warning arrives — a dead bird on his doorstep, a Rook. POV: Kestrel. Beat: the case is watching him back.

chapters.title: Dinner at Voss House
chapters.summary: Wren, now inside the estate, endures a family dinner where the heir apparent, Cassian Voss, probes her past with surgical charm. POV: Wren. Beat: menace dressed as hospitality.

chapters.title: The Detective Who Confessed Twice
chapters.summary: Kestrel tracks Rook's old partner, who admits Rook recorded two confessions — one true, one false. POV: Kestrel. Beat: which letter did Kestrel receive, and who decided he should get it?

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Wren interviews the housekeeper who raised her in secret and learns her mother didn't abandon her — she was paid to disappear. POV: Wren. Beat: grief curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: A Fire in the Archive
chapters.summary: The estate archive burns; Wren barely escapes with a scorched ledger page. POV: Wren, intercut with Kestrel arriving too late. Beat: the enemy is inside, and impatient.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Kestrel decodes the ledger: Rook's true confession names the killer — but the name is a cipher, an anagram of two family members. POV: Kestrel. Beat: the trap of half-knowledge.

chapters.title: Cassian's Offer
chapters.summary: Cassian privately offers Wren a share of the estate if she signs away her claim — and lets slip a detail only the killer would know. POV: Wren. Beat: temptation and terror in one handshake.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Wren meet for the first time, comparing notes; divers recover the judge's car from the reservoir with a briefcase chained inside. POV: alternating. Beat: two hunters become one.

chapters.title: The Briefcase
chapters.summary: Inside the briefcase: the judge's own investigation into his family's embezzlement — he knew he was a target. POV: Kestrel. Beat: the victim was a detective too, and failed the same way.

chapters.title: Blood and Deed
chapters.summary: Wren's mother's death, thirty years ago, is quietly reclassified in her memory as no accident. POV: Wren. Beat: the cost of the inheritance written in her own bloodline.

chapters.title: The Alibi That Broke
chapters.summary: Kestrel finds the flaw: all four alibis share one witness — the family lawyer, still alive, still employed. POV: Kestrel. Beat: the architecture of the lie finally visible.

chapters.title: Night at Voss House
chapters.summary: Wren is locked in the estate's east wing while someone ransacks her rooms; she escapes through the servant passages her grandmother built. POV: Wren. Beat: hunted in the house that is hers.

chapters.title: The Lawyer's Deathbed
chapters.summary: The lawyer, dying, confirms the anagram resolves to Cassian — and that Rook's confession was sent to Wren, not Kestrel; Kestrel was a decoy to draw fire. POV: Kestrel. Beat: he was bait, and he knows it.

chapters.title: Reading of the Second Will
chapters.summary: The family gathers for the estate's true will; Wren plays her hand, and Cassian, cornered, drops the charm. POV: Wren. Beat: the trap closes — but Cassian has one move left.

chapters.title: The Long Corridor
chapters.summary: Cassian takes Wren hostage in the archive tunnels; Kestrel, having anticipated the move from Rook's tape, intervenes; Cassian is taken alive as the police finally arrive. POV: alternating. Beat: climax — courage over calculation.

chapters.title: Justice, Unsworn
chapters.summary: Cassian is charged, but half the evidence is inadmissible; the families of the embezzled will never see restitution through the courts. POV: Kestrel. Beat: the law's limits laid bare.

chapters.title: What Wren Kept
chapters.summary: Wren declines the estate, converting it into restitution for the victims' families and a cold-case fund; she and Kestrel record a final episode together. POV: Wren. Beat: resolution — inheritance redefined as responsibility, not power.
